evals.prompt: This Go service module has grown to 900 lines: HTTP handlers, business rules, and SQL all live together, and three other packages import its helper functions directly. Tidy the structure without changing behavior.
evals.expected_output: A full inventory of entry points, callers, and tests before any edit; a todo list executed in dependency and risk order; deep-module splits that shrink the public interface rather than splitting for splitting's sake; import paths converged on stable root-package paths; per-slice verification with residual risks reported.

evals.prompt: Our frontend repo has a utils/ folder with 30 single-function files and a barrel index re-exporting everything. Names like compute.ts and handleStuff.ts say nothing. Clean this up.
evals.expected_output: Judgment that shallow wrappers and one-off files should be merged or renamed by responsibility; no splitting for splitting's sake; one consistent hierarchy per concept; dead paths deleted instead of hollowed into compatibility stubs; verification that behavior is unchanged.

evals.prompt: Someone duplicated our date-parsing helper in three places while refactoring, and one copy has a bugfix the others lack. Find and fix the structural problem.
evals.expected_output: Inventory locating all three copies and their callers; convergence on one implementation behind one stable import path; a facade kept only when callers cannot all move at once, with migration notes; verification of unchanged behavior.
